summary: Initial POC scoping call to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, timeline, and integration approach (SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, structured output). Agreed to run a dedicated capacity benchmark and to exchange security docs before POC kickoff.
transcript:
00:00 - Maya (Redwood AE): Good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on this account, with Ravi, our SE. Darren, Elena, Tom and Priya from Solstice, thanks for making time.
00:22 - Darren (CTO, Solstice): Yeah thanks, hey all. Quick context, we want to validate whether Redwood can host our inference needs for the new customer support agent — main questions are latency, cost and private deployment options.
01:05 - Maya: Perfect, that's exactly what we want to scope. High level agenda: success criteria, what traffic looks like (QPS, concurrency, typical sequence lengths), benchmarks, timeline, and then the integration approach — SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints and function/tool calling for structured outputs.
02:10 - Elena (Head of ML): For success criteria we're thinking: 1) 99th pct latency under 400ms for 1k daily concurrent users, 2) cost per 1k queries below our current infra cost by at least 30%, and 3) no PII leakage with VPC/KMS enforced.
05:00 - Ravi (Redwood SE): Got it. Quick clarifying Qs — what does a "query" look like? average and 95/99th token lengths? And do you need streaming responses?
08:00 - Tom (Platform Eng): Average prompt is ~120 tokens, responses around 180 tokens. Peak concurrency for the pilot 200 concurrent requests, long-term target 1k concurrent. Streaming desirable but not mandatory.
12:00 - Priya (Security): From security perspective we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS/HSM integration. Also need to validate data residency — EU only for this pilot.
18:00 - Maya: We'll share SOC2 and the security whitepaper; Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem options, and we have KMS integrations. For EU residency we can pin to EU region or run a private deployment.
24:00 - Ravi: For sizing, couple of notes: continuous batching and KV cache can reduce token cost for repeated context, but it changes latency tradeoffs. For 200 concurrency pilot we recommend a small dedicated pool (we call Redwood Dedicated) — gives predictable throughput and isolation. For the 1k target we'll size based on benchmark results.
30:00 - Elena: On benchmarks — can you run a runbook? We can provide a representative dataset (1000 sessions) and success test scripts. We'll want both latency percentiles and cost per token numbers. Also functional correctness: the structured output fields must match schema and tool calls need to be reliable.
36:00 - Ravi: Yes we usually run a three-stage benchmark: 1) smoke in hosted env, 2) dedicated capacity run with representative load, 3) long-run to measure KV cache and batching effects. We'll use Redwood SDKs or OpenAI-compatible endpoints depending on your stack. We can run function calling patterns — note that our function/tool calling supports structured JSON output but transcription sometimes shows names like Redwood Dediated in earlier logs, so we'll validate output schema strictly.
42:00 - Tom: Integration question — we use an internal assistant built on OpenAI-compatible API wrappers. If Redwood provides OpenAI-compatible endpoints that's simpler; otherwise SDK clients are fine as long as auth (SSO/service keys) and regional endpoints are supported.
42:45 - Maya: We do provide OpenAI-compatible endpoints and first-class SDKs in Python/TS. The function calling semantics are compatible but there are some behavior differences around n-best and structured output; we'll share best-practices for deterministic JSON outputs and schema validation.
44:10 - Priya: On audits and logs — can we get per-request audit logs and token-level redaction?
44:40 - Maya: Yes, audit logs and per-request tracing exist in Redwood Console. For PII we recommend their optional redaction layer and customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. We'll include a runbook for KMS/HSM integration.
45:20 - Elena: Timeline — we want to kick off POC next week if possible. Ideally 2-week pilot: week 1 benchmarks and tuning, week 2 soak and validation.
46:05 - Ravi: That timeline looks feasible. We'll need your dataset and success criteria locked by Monday 2026-12-20 so we can schedule a dedicated cluster, run benchmarks on 12/22 and share results 12/23.
47:30 - Maya: Recap / next steps: 1) Solstice to send dataset, success criteria and PII constraints (Elena/Priya) by 2026-12-20; 2) Maya will send pricing and dedicated capacity proposal by 2026-12-21; 3) Ravi will prepare benchmark harness and test credentials and run the dedicated run on 2026-12-22; 4) follow-up POC kickoff/bench result review 2026-12-23. Thanks everyone, we'll send calendar invites and the security package after this call.
47:58 - Darren: Thanks, appreciate it.
48:00 - Call ended.
